BWMX.notes: EPS is BASIC (the release gives no diluted EPS), in nominal pesos. Net income: Q3 390.3 vs 314.2 million pesos (+24.2%); nine months 1,066.2 vs 792.9 million (+34.5%). Shares rose (39.5 vs 37.3 million weighted in Q3) because shares were issued for the acquisition. IMPORTANT for the growth test: the jump is acquisition-driven. Tupperware Latam was acquired in June 2026 and consolidated from then (Q3 revenue 1,375.8 million pesos, 28.5% of the group); Q3 revenue +43.1% in total but only +2.3% excluding Tupperware (existing report), Jafra brand -2.8%, Betterware brand +9.7%. The company's 'comparable organic EBITDA' grew 2.8% in nine months. The comparison is also flattered by a 108.8 million peso unrealised derivative loss in 9M 2025 (none in 2026), partly offset by FX (-11.6 million loss vs +73.2 million gain), 43 million of non-recurring acquisition costs in 2026 and a 34-35 million tax benefit in 2025; the company gives no adjusted net income, so 'adjusted' is null. Q3 effective tax rate 45.8% (company calls it temporary). Do not use the headline 'combined' nine-month EPS of 45.42 (+114.2%): it adds Tupperware's pre-acquisition profit. Within Tupperware, B2B sales (111.8 million pesos in Q3 2025) went to zero and Argentina and US sales fell from 178.0 to 23.4 million; the release calls these extraordinary prior-year non-direct-channel sales discontinued after the acquisition - they were never in Betterware's own history, so not 'departed'. Quarterly dividend approved: 250 million pesos (0.3424 US dollars per share).

MA.notes: Primary: SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1.
